components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; white-space: nowrap; border-radius: 0.375rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; height: 36px; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; background: var(--brand-primary, #1E40AF); color: #f8fafc; border: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 1px 2px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); transition: background-color 150ms; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(from var(--brand-primary, #1E40AF) l c h / 0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 0 0 1px #94a3b8; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { pointer-events: none; opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Outline Button

narrative.overview:
An open, inviting surface alive with activity. Imagine a well-maintained campus bulletin board: club flyers layered with personality, event cards pinned with purpose, clear headings that draw your eye to what matters. The information is dense but never cluttered, colorful but never chaotic. Every piece earns its pushpin.

This system serves three audiences at once. Students scanning for their next club between classes need fast visual hierarchy and scannable layouts. Officers managing rosters need efficient bulk actions and unmistakable status indicators. Platform admins checking in occasionally need clear admin navigation without cluttering anyone else's view. The design responds to each without compromising the others.

The visual language is Restrained in the product sense: tinted neutrals carry 90% of the surface, with the configurable brand color appearing only on primary actions, active states, and navigation identity. This restraint is strategic. Since the brand color swaps per university deployment, every element must look intentional whether the accent is navy blue, forest green, or crimson.
keyCharacteristics: Configurable accent on a slate neutral base
Cards always carry a light ambient shadow, gaining strength on hover
System font stack throughout. Hierarchy through weight and size contrast, not display fonts
Status colors (green, yellow, red) are the only fixed palette beyond neutrals
Compact density: page gaps at 24px, card padding at 16-24px, form groups at 16px

rules.name: The Configurable Accent Rule
rules.body: The brand color is the only hue that changes per deployment. All accent usage must trace back to var(--brand-primary).

rules.name: The Always-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Cards never sit flat on the page. Even at rest, the ambient shadow separates them from the background. Hover intensifies the lift; it never introduces it from zero.

rules.name: The Size Floor Rule
rules.body: No text below 12px (0.75rem). Badge and metadata are the floor; everything else is 14px or above.

dos: Do use var(--brand-primary) for all accent-colored elements so white-label recoloring works with a single CSS variable change.
Do give cards ambient shadow at rest and medium shadow on hover.
Do use status colors (green, yellow, red) consistently for membership state, RSVP response, and validation feedback.
Do keep body text at 14px (0.875rem) and above.
Do use the 12px radius for cards and 6px for inputs and buttons.
Do use system font stack. No custom font loading.
Do test dark mode for every new component.
donts: Don't use emojis, illustrations, or confetti animations.
Don't create hero-metric dashboards with big numbers and gradient accents.
Don't use glassmorphism, gradient text, or side-stripe borders.
Don't build identical card grids (same-sized icon + heading + text repeated).
Don't hardcode colors outside the token system.
Don't use display fonts in UI labels, buttons, or data.
Don't use spinners for content loading states.
